purdue_ext_ho8wa.citable_for: Purdue HO-8-W (B. Rosie Lerner and Michael N. Dana; revised 4/01): planting cucurbits in hills. The only page measured for PLA-673 that sizes the mound: "To form a hill, mound soil to make a low, broad hill about 8-10 inches high." Also: 4-6 seeds per hill, hills 4-8 feet apart by variety, thin to 2-3 plants per hill. No hill diameter is stated. The document's header prints HO-8-W; the edustore filename is HO-8-W-A. Parent portal entry: purdue_ext.

csu_ext_cucurbits_07609.title: Cucumbers, Pumpkins, Squash, and Melons
csu_ext_cucurbits_07609.citable_for: CSU Fact Sheet 7.609 (J. Murgel, C.W. Basham, J.E. Ells; published November 1999, reviewed August 2025): cucurbits "are usually planted in hills or mounds so excess water drains away from the seedlings"; five or six seeds together in hills 4 to 6 feet apart; thin each hill to the two or three strongest seedlings. States no mound height. Parent portal entry: csu_ext.

nmsu_ext_cr457.name: NMSU Circular 457 -- Home Vegetable Gardening in New Mexico
nmsu_ext_cr457.title: Home Vegetable Gardening in New Mexico
nmsu_ext_cr457.publisher: New Mexico State University, College of Agricultural, Consumer and Environmental Sciences, Cooperative Extension Service
nmsu_ext_cr457.citable_for: NMSU Circular 457 (revised by Stephanie Walker and Israel Joukhadar): the hill method of direct seeding ("use a hoe to make a hole in the soil, then drop four or five seeds in the bottom of the hole"; "thin to one to three of the most vigorous seedlings after emergence when plants have their first true leaves"), the crops often planted in hills (squash, melons, cucumbers, corn, chile), and squash hill spacings (bush 24-45 in. apart in rows 36-60 in.; vining 36-96 in. apart in rows 72-96 in.). Companion: Circular 457-B (nmsu_ext_cr457b). Parent portal entry: nmsu_ext.

uga_b577_home_gardening.name: UGA Extension Bulletin 577 -- Home Gardening

uga_b577_home_gardening.citable_for: UGA Bulletin 577, the full Home Gardening bulletin page (distinct from its one-page Home Garden Planting Chart PDF, which is uga_b577). Defines planting in hills against drills: "a drill is a single row of plants spaced more-or-less evenly. a hill is a cluster of plants, not a mound of soil."
